terms.meaning: Canonical order entity is the reserved PostgreSQL table order. The canonical analytical grain is order.id.
A physical order row whose order.created_at falls inside the requested IST interval. Plain placed-order metrics do not exclude later-cancelled orders.

A placed order that is not fully cancelled. Full cancellation means native order.status is canceled/cancelled OR non-null order.zoho_order_status is CANCELED/CANCELLED. order.canceled_at is not canonical cancellation truth.
Normally the canonical analytical variant grain line_item.variant_id / product_variant.id. product_variant.sku is only the literal stored SKU string when explicitly requested.
Product-level analytical grain is product.id / product_variant.product_id. Product requests roll applicable variants to product grain.
Variant-level analytical grain is line_item.variant_id / product_variant.id. Display titles do not define analytical identity.
order.zoho_order_status. It is distinct from order.status, order.fulfillment_status, order.payment_status and fulfillment.delivery_status.
By default in Mill-it Ops, operationally fulfilled means order.zoho_order_status is FULFILLED. Native fulfillment status is separate and must be explicitly requested.
Canonical actual custom delivery state is fulfillment.delivery_status. order.delivery_status is not authoritative actual-delivery truth.
customer.id / order.customer_id is the canonical analytical customer identifier. Customer behavior is based on qualifying purchases unless another population is explicitly requested.
Sum of line_item.quantity minus preaggregated partial cancelled quantity, floored at zero, among qualifying orders. Product or variant grain is determined separately by the request.
Historical placed-order monetary value based on the selected applicable order-level payment when supported. It is distinct from qualifying, captured and net-collected value.
Placed order value for a qualifying order reduced by applicable partial-cancellation value. It is an operational metric, not accounting revenue.
Sum of qualifying order value divided by count of qualifying orders over the same population.
Selected applicable order-level payment amount for orders whose canonical order.payment_status is captured.
refund_request.refund_amount where the verified refund request status is processed. payment.amount_refunded and native refund rows are not the current canonical processed-refund source.
Operational approximation equal to captured value minus processed refunds. It is not accounting-recognized revenue.

AOV is not a single universal metric. Use placed AOV, qualifying AOV or realized AOV according to the requested population/value definition. Generic sales-oriented AOV should use the explicitly supported qualifying AOV definition.
A customer population selected by validated qualifying-order frequency, recency or inactivity conditions. Eligibility-window counting and latest qualifying activity may require separate calculations.
Rolling six-calendar-month lookback from the validated historical as-of boundary unless the request explicitly asks for complete calendar months.
Six fully completed calendar months. Rust resolves the exact IST boundaries.
Rust-generated predictive output using complete historical observations. Qwen supplies semantic intent and historical-query requirements but does not invent forecast values.
Month-over-month means sequential calendar-month comparison, week-over-week means sequential calendar-week comparison, and year-over-year means matching comparable spans one year apart.
